alignments.note: The English preposition of the discontinuous *point unto ... what time* realizes the Greek preposition under rule 36; the verb keeps *did point*.
*what manner of* is one English expression for the single interrogative; *manner of* is a rule 7 completion and rule 17 keeps the head on the interrogative word.

One Greek noun governs both interrogatives and the ASV repeats *time*, italicising the first; rule 11 makes that markup evidence rather than an `added` verdict, and rule 15 permits the discontinuous unit. Head on the unsupplied occurrence. This is one source token scoping a coordination, which the corpus folds — TIT.1.15, REV.4.11, REV.19.16 — and not the resumptive apposition of 1PE.1.19, where the supplied phrase follows a completed phrase whose every token is already spent and is `added` as at JHN.1.9 and REV.16.12. A defensible alternative attaches the supplied *time* to the first interrogative.
Rule 17 heads on the lexical verb rather than the auxiliary.

The article precedes the noun it governs across the interposed prepositional phrase (rule 57), so under rule 31 it takes the determiner together with the supplied relativizer, headed on *the*, and the noun stands bare.
A prepositional predicate carries the supplied copula under rules 31 and 53.
Rule 17: for a source noun rendered *of + noun*, the noun is the head.
The supplied *when* and *it* are rule 7 helpers on the participle; rule 17 heads on the lexical verb.
The article governs the noun across the interposed prepositional phrase (rule 57) and takes the English determiner under rule 19; no relative clause is supplied here.
The ASV renders the goal preposition by *of*; rule 36 keeps that English preposition on the Greek preposition rather than absorbing it into the noun.
As with the earlier article, this one precedes its noun across a prepositional phrase, so rule 31 gives it the discontinuous *the ... that*, headed on *the*.

The ASV verbalizes the prepositional phrase, and rule 62 puts the supplied lexical verb on the preposition it realizes; *should follow* answers to *after*. Rule 45 is not in question, since the ASV spreads the phrase over words answering to each token.
The demonstrative is realized by the pronoun *them* in the verbalized rendering.
